svg.text: Traits: how a write evaluates them and how they act on each other
left: the write path of the entity type (entity-type, trait-container) · right: what a trait sees and may do at each step
create
initialTraitValues: each valued
trait.initialize(input, create)
identity trait → businessKey
change { create, after }
run · command
applyTraitOperations →
traitCommands: trait.operation
({ value, input }) returns
{ command, value }; needs revision
run · plan
process, in a transaction:
trait.operation → { operations,
output, commit }; commit:false
= preview of the whole write
delete · derive
delete: change { delete, before }
derive: backfill after a rule
changed, commands as one
trait change
1 applyChange: revision check
input.revision ≠ before.revision → throw conflict
2 guardRequest: guardTraits, then the guards slot (the request)
for each trait, in the order of entity-traits: its hook guard({ entityType, key, configuration, change })
read and trace only; throws to refuse; decides from change.operation
then the fills of the slot guards that are on the operation
3 deriveData (not on delete): a queue of operations, to a fixed point
dirty derives are consulted one at a time, in trait order: derive({ …, record, command })
→ an ordered list of operations [{ key, operation, input }], [] when its value is right
its operations run in order, each on the current value; the command is applied to the record
a command on a key makes the derives that dependsOn it dirty again
ends when none is dirty and the queue is empty; over maxDerivationSteps: derivation-limit
dependsOn is declared in the trait use · a derive is idempotent, read and trace only
dirty again
4 guardResult: the slot resultGuards (not on delete)
the change carries the commands of the whole write, requested and derived, in order
after = the entity as it would be stored · read and trace only · throws to refuse
nothing is written yet, so a refusal needs no rollback
5 store: the change becomes values of keys
create: after, as derived · trait: set each key to its command.value on before (whole value)
delete: remove before · all commands of the change land in one revision
command is metadata: stored nowhere, seen by guards, reactions, events
inTransaction (rollback on any failure)
6 entity-database write
store writes only if the record is still at the revision it read, else conflict
7 reactTraits, then the reactions slot
for each trait: react({ entityType, key, configuration, change }), change.after = written record
change.commands include the derived ones · may write other entities; a failure rolls back
then the fills of the slot reactions, with the written change
8 return the viewed record
each trait view maps only its own value; the stored record is not what callers see
Writes are optimistic
every write names the revision it applies to
guards decide on before, the store checks it again
Guard: one trait decides on any change
the change carries the commands of every trait
state refuses update of body outside its states,
with no fill: the behaviour travels with the trait
Derive: traits feed one another by what they read
a derive declares the keys it reads: dependsOn,
the only ordering mechanism; trait order breaks ties
a request is never stale: one derive at a time
a derive can request state.transition, same change
a trait may exist only to trigger another's operation
Guards run twice
request: before any work (access, visibility)
result: what a derive added, such as an owner
the preview (commit: false) runs the fold and both
One change, one revision
commands from the caller, plan operations and
derives are written together; no history is kept,
a feature that needs one persists it in a reaction
React: a trait acts on other entities
an amending trait writes the amendments,
inside the same transaction; if one fails,
the write and what it created roll back
How traits reach each other
body
value of key body
state
status, transitions
validations
derives violations
amending
react writes other entities
guard refuses body operations
derive asks transition (operations)
derive reads the record by kind, with the earlier commands applied
Before any write: a trait use is formed
key → { trait, configuration } is the deep union of the contributions:
fixed.traits of the kind chain · traits of the entity type · fills of the slot traits
the same path with another value is a conflict, nothing replaces anything
a trait may take over a key (versioned-body takes body)
Reading across traits
never by path data.<key>: $func/entity-trait-value({ record, kind })
finds the use whose trait is an instance of the kind
the owner of a trait offers its own reader (record-state, record-body)
a view sees only its own value; hooks see the change of all traits
